steps: Entrepreneurship is the process of identifying an opportunity, organising resources and starting a business to provide a product or service.
Entrepreneurs create jobs by employing people and by creating work for suppliers and other businesses.
They introduce new products, services and ways of working. This innovation can improve people’s lives and make businesses more productive.
Successful businesses produce and sell goods and services, helping increase income and economic activity in a country.
For example, a person who starts an online business selling locally made products can provide income for themselves and employment for others.
An entrepreneur who develops a useful mobile application or an improved farming tool can solve a problem while introducing an innovation to the market.
items.finalAnswer: Entrepreneurship supports economic growth by creating jobs, income and useful innovations that solve problems.

steps: Market research tools, such as online surveys, website analytics and social-media polls, help a business understand customers, their needs and competing products.
The business uses this information to decide what to sell, who its customers are and how to price and improve its products.
Online marketing tools, such as a website, social-media pages, email and online advertisements, help the business reach and communicate with potential customers.
The business can use the findings from market research to make its online advertisements and messages relevant to the customers most likely to buy.
An e-commerce platform displays products, accepts orders and payments, and helps the business manage sales online.
Together, these tools allow a business to learn about customers, promote suitable products, make sales online and use customer feedback to improve its service.
For example, a bookstore can use a survey to learn which textbooks students need, promote those books on social media and sell them through its online store.
items.finalAnswer: Market research identifies customer needs, online marketing reaches customers, and e-commerce platforms turn interest into online sales.

steps: Design thinking is a human-centred process for understanding a problem and developing, testing and improving a solution.
Empathise: learn about the people who have the problem by observing them and listening to their needs.
Define: clearly state the problem that needs to be solved.
Ideate: think of and compare different possible solutions.
Prototype: make a simple model or early version of the best idea.
Test: let users try the prototype, collect their feedback and improve the solution.
For example, to help farmers in rural Pakistan, a team could first visit farms and talk to farmers about difficulties with watering crops.
The team could define the problem as a lack of timely information about when and how much to water crops.
It could suggest ideas such as a simple Urdu-language mobile service giving local weather and irrigation advice.
The team could make a basic version of the service and test it with a small group of farmers.
Farmers’ feedback could then be used to improve the instructions and make the service easier to use on basic mobile phones.
items.finalAnswer: Design thinking uses empathy, problem definition, ideas, prototypes and testing to create and improve solutions for users.

steps: Business idea: establish an online bookstore serving students in the local area, with textbooks, exam guides, past papers and affordable supplementary reading.
Target customers: students in nearby schools, colleges and tuition centres, and parents or teachers who buy books for them.
Market research: ask students and teachers which books they use, how often they buy books, what price range they can afford and whether they prefer new or used books.
Use short online surveys, conversations at schools or tuition centres, and social-media polls to collect this information.
Student reading habits: check which subjects and exam guides are most requested, when students buy books during the school year, and whether they also read novels or other books for enjoyment.
Competitor analysis: compare local bookshops and online booksellers by checking their book selection, prices, delivery areas, delivery times and customer service.
Identify an opportunity by offering convenient local delivery, clear prices and the required course books in one place.
Use the research results to choose the initial stock and update it when students’ needs change.
items.finalAnswer: Research local students’ reading and buying habits, compare competing booksellers, and stock the books students need at suitable prices.

steps: The bookstore will earn income mainly by selling books through its website or online store.
It can sell new textbooks, exam preparation books, stationery bundles and selected supplementary reading material.
Where suitable books are available, the store can also sell second-hand books at lower prices to students.
The selling price should cover the purchase cost of each book and other business costs, while remaining affordable for local students.
The store can offer delivery for an additional fee or provide free delivery for orders above a stated amount, if the delivery cost is covered.
It may offer school or tuition-centre group orders at a negotiated price to encourage larger purchases.
For example, before each school term, the store could prepare subject-wise book bundles and sell them to students who need a complete set.
The business should record sales, costs and profit regularly and adjust its stock and prices according to demand.
items.finalAnswer: The bookstore will earn revenue from book and bundle sales, with possible delivery charges and group orders.

steps: Create a simple online store with clear book titles, prices, availability, delivery information and contact details.
Use social-media pages popular with local students and parents to announce new stock, discounts and examination-season offers.
Post useful content, such as reading suggestions, book lists for each class and reminders about required textbooks.
Use paid online advertisements targeted to people in the local area, where the budget allows.
Share the store’s catalogue and order information through school, tuition-centre and community groups, with permission.
Encourage satisfied customers to leave honest reviews and share their experience with other students.
Send email or messaging updates to customers who have agreed to receive them, especially when requested books become available.
Check which posts and advertisements result in enquiries and orders, then focus on the most effective methods.
items.finalAnswer: Promote the bookstore through a clear online store, local social media, useful book content, targeted advertisements and customer reviews.

steps: Start with a limited stock of books that local students request most often, and expand the selection after checking sales and customer feedback.
Display prices in Pakistani rupees and state whether delivery charges are included.
Offer practical local payment choices, such as cash on delivery where available and a suitable digital payment method.
Give customers an estimated delivery time and use a reliable local courier or delivery service.
Provide a telephone or messaging contact so students and parents can ask about book editions, stock and orders.
For example, the store could survey students at a nearby school, list the most requested class textbooks online and arrange delivery within the surrounding area.
These steps keep the bookstore useful to local students while helping the owner manage costs and build trust.
items.finalAnswer: Use local student research, rupee pricing, convenient payment and reliable delivery to make the bookstore practical in Pakistan.

steps: Example: a local solar-panel installation business in Pakistan that supplies and installs solar systems for homes, shops and small farms.
It supports SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy by helping customers use electricity generated from sunlight.
It can support SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth by employing and training installers, electricians and sales staff.
Its services can help customers reduce reliance on electricity generated from fossil fuels, supporting SDG 13: Climate Action.
Social sustainability: access to a suitable solar system can help households and small businesses obtain a more dependable electricity supply, subject to system size and sunlight.

Environmental sustainability: solar power produces electricity without direct emissions during operation, although the panels and batteries must be manufactured and responsibly managed at the end of their useful life.
Economic sustainability: the business earns income from sales and installation, creates local jobs and may help customers reduce electricity costs over time.
The business should provide honest advice, safe installation and responsible arrangements for repairing or disposing of equipment.
items.finalAnswer: A local solar-installation business can support clean energy, local employment and lower-emission electricity while operating as a sustainable business.
